title: Joins, key validation and duplicate fanout
outcome: Validate relational assumptions in DataFrames joins and reconcile totals before and after a merge.

exercises.title: Trace the duplicate pair
exercises.task: Join the duplicated right-side entity 1 observations.
exercises.expected: The left entity 1 weight appears twice.
exercises.answer: Join multiplicity can inflate a sum even when every individual match is syntactically valid.

exercises.title: Enforce a lookup contract
exercises.task: Require uniqueness on the right lookup key.
exercises.answer: An executable cardinality check prevents an unintended many-to-many relationship from passing silently.

exercises.title: Aggregate at a declared grain
exercises.task: Sum observations to one row per entity before the join.
exercises.expected: Two entity rows and weight total 300 are preserved.
exercises.hint: Choose an aggregation that matches the analytical question.
exercises.answer: Preaggregation is a semantic decision, not a universal repair for duplicates.

exercises.title: Choose missing-key behavior
exercises.task: Compare equal and nonmatching missing-key policies.
exercises.expected: The fixture yields 1 or 0 matched rows.
exercises.hint: Unknown keys do not imply identical entities.
exercises.answer: The policy must reflect the data model and should be reported with excluded counts.

exercises.title: Inspect unmatched keys
exercises.task: Use an outer join with an origin indicator.
exercises.expected: The fixture exposes left-only, both and right-only rows.
exercises.answer: A row-count total is not enough to explain which entities failed to match.

exercises.title: Avoid cosmetic deduplication
exercises.task: Remove duplicate output rows without reviewing their cause.
exercises.hint: Reconcile the intended input/output grain first.
exercises.answer: Distinct operations can conceal a modeling error and need their own justified rule.
